name: Daoine sídhe

attributes.name: barrow
attributes.attribute: ancient mound home of the fairies

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Daoine Sidhe is an Irish term for fairy folk. The name means folk from the mound. These figures were once deities. The Tuatha Dé Danann were reduced to folktale figures. They came to live in ancient barrows. They also lived in hillforts. They used other prehistoric monuments of Ireland. People used many flattering names to win their good will. The fairies could be amoral and mischievous. People called them The Good Folk, daoine maithe. People called them The Gentry, daoine uaisle. Some simply called them Them. The mound was their traditional home.
objective: This record documents Daoine sídhe, an Irish euphemism for fairy folk meaning folk from the mound.
key_results: Daoine sídhe means folk from the mound.
The diminished Tuatha Dé Danann live in barrows and hillforts.
Flattering names such as daoine maithe aimed to win fairy good will.
The Good Folk and The Gentry are alternate euphemisms.
